title: Total of the Left-Hand Leaves
statement:
You get the root of a binary tree. A left leaf is a node with no children that is the left child of its parent.

Return the sum of the values of all left leaves. The root has no parent, so it is never a left leaf, even when it is alone. Return 0 if there are none.

examples.why: The left leaves are 1 (under 2) and 6 (under 7). 9 is a leaf, but a right one.
A lone root is a leaf, but it is nobody's left child.
2 is a left child but not a leaf, since it has the child 4. Both leaves, 4 and 3, are right children.

hints: A node cannot tell on its own whether it is a left leaf. Who knows which side it hangs on?
Either pass a flag isLeft down the recursion, or let each parent check its own left child: is it there, and does it have no children?
Leaf test: !node.left && !node.right. Add the value only when that holds and the node came in through a left link.

explain.intuition:
Being a "left leaf" depends on two facts: the node has no children, and it is the left child of its parent. The node knows the first fact, but only the parent knows the second. So either the parent checks its left child directly, or the recursion carries a flag that says which side we came from.

With the flag, the rule is short: a leaf reached with isLeft = true contributes its value, every other leaf contributes 0, and an inner node returns the sum of its two subtrees, calling the left with true and the right with false. The root starts with false, which handles the lone-root case.
steps: Define walk(node, isLeft). A null node returns 0.
If the node has no children, return its value when isLeft is true, else 0.
pitfalls: Counting every left child, even ones that have children of their own.
Counting a lone root as a left leaf. It has no parent, so the answer is 0.
Only checking the left child and not walking into it when it is not a leaf. Its own subtree can hold more left leaves, like the 7 under 5 in [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, null, 6, null, null, 7].

complexity.space: O(h) for the recursion, O(w) for the BFS

solutions.title: DFS with a which-side flag
solutions.idea: Carry whether the current node is a left child. Leaves reached through a left link contribute their value.

solutions.title: Level-order walk, parent checks its left child
solutions.idea: Visit nodes with a queue. Each node looks at its own left child and adds it if that child is a leaf.

followups: Return the sum of left leaves at the deepest level only.
Do it with O(1) extra space using a Morris traversal. What extra care does the left-leaf check need?
